transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… yeah. I guess I came in because I’ve been feeling pretty bad about myself lately. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but I keep thinking I’ve let my family down, especially with the mortgage we took on. And then at work, even a small mistake makes me feel like it proves I’m useless… like I kind of deserve whatever happens after that. Is that… the kind of thing you mean?
Have these feelings of being useless or not good enough been happening most days, and do they sometimes come up even when things are going okay?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I try not to dwell on it, and some days I can kind of push it aside, but it’s there a lot. Even if things are basically okay, I’ll still start thinking I’ve messed things up for my family with the mortgage, or if I make some tiny mistake at work it feels like proof that I’m just… not good enough. Like I deserve the fallout, I guess. Is that what you mean?
How long have you been feeling this way? Have these thoughts been present for weeks, months, or longer?

Um… it’s been longer than just a few weeks. I guess if I’m being honest, these depressed, guilty stretches have been around for… maybe about a year and a couple months. Not every single minute, but over that whole time, yeah. Is that the kind of timeframe you’re asking for?
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, like activities or hobbies you used to like?

Yeah… maybe a little. I don’t want to overstate it, because I still get through work and everything, but I’m not really like I used to be. I used to joke around with the regulars more, and after shifts I’d text my brother about random stuff.

Lately I mostly just keep my face kind of straight, say what I need to say, and leave it at that. And messages… I’ll see them and just let them sit, not because I’m mad, I just don’t really feel that pull to answer. Is that what you mean?
Have you noticed that you feel more tired than usual or that you don’t have the same energy, even when you haven’t been doing anything particularly draining?

I’m not sure, honestly. I mean, waiting tables is tiring anyway, so I kind of assume it’s just that. I haven’t really noticed a big change where I’m exhausted for no reason… maybe some days I’m slower getting going, but I don’t know if that counts. I’m sorry, is that helpful?
Have you stopped doing or lost interest in activities that you used to enjoy, even things that were important to you?

I wouldn’t say I’ve completely stopped everything, exactly… but yeah, some things don’t feel the same. Like I used to joke around with the regulars at work more, and I’d usually text my brother after shifts, just little stuff.

Now I kind of just keep my face straight, say what I need to say, and go quiet. And I let messages sit there, not because I don’t care about him or anything… I just don’t feel that pull to answer. I don’t know if that counts as losing interest, but it’s definitely different.
Have you noticed that you no longer take pleasure or interest in things you used to enjoy, even small things that used to make you feel good?

Yeah… I guess, in small ways. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but I used to kind of enjoy joking with the regulars at work, and now I mostly just keep a straight face and say what I need to say.

And after shifts I used to text my brother about random things, nothing important, but lately I’ll see his messages and just leave them there. It’s not that I don’t care… I just don’t feel that pull to answer like I used to. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed yourself moving or thinking more slowly than usual lately, like it takes more effort to get things done or you feel physically slowed down?

A little, yeah… I mean, I didn’t really think of it that way at first. At work people have kind of pointed out that I’ll either pace around and check the same tables or receipts more than I need to, or I’ll be the opposite and move really slow.

Like grabbing menus or walking over to the POS will take me longer than it should. I don’t think I’m trying to be difficult or anything… it just happens. Is that what you mean by slowed down?
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently, like eating more or less than usual or losing or gaining weight without trying?

Yeah… somewhat. I don’t think it’s been, like, dramatic or anything, but my eating’s been kind of inconsistent.

Some weeks at work I barely touch the staff meal, even if I know I should eat. Then other nights I get home and I’ll just eat whatever’s around in the kitchen, not even because I’m really hungry exactly… more like it helps me feel settled. I haven’t been trying to change my weight or anything. Is that the kind of change you’re asking about?
Have you had episodes like this before, where you felt down, guilty, or lost interest in things, or is this the first time you’ve felt this way for this long?

It’s not the first time, no… I mean, I don’t want to overstate it, but these down or guilty stretches, and not really feeling interested in things, have been around for a while.

If I’m counting it right, it’s been about a year and a couple months altogether… maybe around a year and two months that I’ve felt like this on and off. Does that make sense?
Before this current time, have you ever had a period where you felt down, guilty, or lost interest in things for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t always like calling it that, because I can still show up to work and do what I’m supposed to do, but most days there’s been this kind of heavy, empty feeling in my chest.

Like I’m carrying plates and smiling at tables because that’s the job, not because I really feel anything good. That’s been there in stretches before too… if that answers what you mean.
Before this current time, have you had more than one separate period where you felt down, guilty, or lost interest in things for at least a couple of weeks at a time?

Yeah… I think there’s been more than one stretch like that. I don’t know if I’ve tracked it perfectly, but it’s happened in separate periods where most days I get that heavy, empty feeling in my chest.

I still go to work and do the smiling and carrying plates and all that, so I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is… but it feels like I’m just going through the motions, not really feeling anything good. Is that what you mean by separate periods?

Before this current time, have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks where you felt down or lost interest in things nearly every day, and it was bad enough that it affected your daily life, like work or family?

Yeah… I guess it has affected things, even if I try not to let it show.

There’ve been times I almost missed shifts, and I’ve made some mistakes with mortgage paperwork that I really should’ve caught. At work, keeping up with the POS reports and inventory has been harder than it used to be. I’m still doing it, mostly, but it feels like I’m slipping, and then I start worrying that if I mess up enough I could lose the job… and then maybe the condo too.

And I’ve kind of pulled back from my brother and people at work. Not completely, but enough that they’ve noticed I’m not really myself. I don’t know if that counts as “bad enough,” but… yeah, it’s been affecting my life.
Have you ever had times when you felt so good, energetic, or irritable that people noticed a big change in your behavior, or where you needed less sleep but still had lots of energy?

I don’t think so… not in a big way like that.

I mean, I have better days sometimes, or days where I’m more wired from stress, but I don’t think people would say I was suddenly a totally different person or anything. And I don’t really remember needing way less sleep and still feeling great or full of energy.

If there’s a specific kind of thing you mean, I can try to think harder, but… I don’t think that’s been me.
